textbookText: Q. From what height a block of ice must be dropped so that it can completely melt. It is assumed that 20% of energy of fall is retained by ice. [L = 3.36105 Jkg-1, g = 10 ms-2]
Solution: Here,
Acceleration due to gravity (g) = 10 ms-2
Latent heat of fusion of ice (L) = 3.36105 Jkg-1
Suppose h be the height from where a block of ice is dropped so that it can melt by taking
20% of its loss in P.E. ( = m g h) as latent heat. Let m is mass of ice and g is acceleration
due to gravity.
According to the question,
m L = 20% of m g h
Hence, the block of ice should be dropped from the height of 1.7×105 m.

During boiling, liquid takes certain amount of heat as latent heat. The temperature at which liquid changes into vapour (gas) is called the boiling point. Different objects have different values of boiling point. Boiling point of water is 100oC at 760mm of Hg pressure.

Effect of Pressure on Boiling Point Even for a single object, the boiling point varies according to the pressure exerted on it. The actual boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which the saturated vapor pressure of the liquid becomes equal to the external (atmospheric) pressure on its surface. The boiling point of a liquid increases with an increase in pressure, and decreases with a decrease in pressure. Further, pressure decreases with an increase in altitude, and increases with a decrease in altitude. Therefore, the boiling point is a function of pressure, which, in turn, is a function of altitude. For example, water boils at a lower temperature in Solukhumbu than in Birgunj, and rice is cooked faster in a pressure cooker than in an open pot.

11.15 Evaporation We feel cold when we spray perfume on our body. Similarly, we experience a cooling sensation in our mouth when we eat Halls. Can you explain the physics behind these phenomena? Both cases involve the cooling effect of evaporation.
A slow and silent process of conversion of liquid into vapour at all temperature below its boiling point is called evaporation. Evaporation takes place from the surface of a liquid.

During evaporation, molecules escape from the surface of a liquid, and convert into vapour. Those molecules take necessary latent heat of conversion from the neighboring molecules and hence the temperature of the remaining mass of liquid decreases. This effect is called cooling effect of evaporation.
